- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00 or +0.67 with recent spike), model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., -1.00 or -0.67) after a peak, model often lags — delay correction by 1–2 days and adjust downward gradually.
- High news volume (≥2.0) correlates with overestimation — apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias if news volume >1.0 in last 3 days.
- If sentiment change is negative and forecast is rising, model often misreads trend — reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 in next 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day window — if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is flat (±0.00) and forecast is rising, model often overestimates — cap forecast at 10% above recent 5-day average.
- Overshoot after sentiment spike: if sentiment rises >0.67 and forecast >+5% above prior peak, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day for 3 days.
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is low, model often underestimates — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias if sentiment <0.00 and forecast <5% below recent 5-day average.
